title: Are You Still Committed?
paragraphs:
Are You Still Committed?
Luke 9:62
Jesus did not whisper this.
He said it like a blade.
“No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” — Luke 9:62

That verse is not for the half-awake.
It is for the person who said yes to God… then started missing Egypt.

You prayed the prayer.
You made the vow.
You wept at the altar.
But now?

You keep glancing back.
Back to the old appetite.
Back to the old relationship.
Back to the old version of you that Jesus died to bury.
And here’s the tension:
You cannot plow straight while staring behind you.

That is not commitment.
That is hesitation dressed like devotion.
But here’s what we miss…

Jesus is not calling us to perfection without struggle.
He is calling us to undivided surrender.

The issue is not that the disciple feels temptation.
The issue is that his heart is still negotiating with the past.

Beloved, the Kingdom is too weighty for casual followers.
Christ did not shed His blood so we could live with one hand on the plow and one hand holding onto our idols.
This is where grace walks in.

If you have looked back, repent.
If your fire has cooled, return.
If your commitment has cracked, run back to the cross.

Jesus does not just expose divided hearts.
He redeems them.

Peter failed.
Peter wept.
Peter was restored.

So this is not a verse of hopelessness.
It is a wake-up call wrapped in mercy.

Fix your eyes forward.
Not on your failures.
Not on your cravings.
On Christ.
Because the same Savior who said, “Don’t look back,” is the Savior who gives power to keep going.
